answer: Proof of storage makes each identity carry its own weight: on joining, an agent is assigned a unique, random shard of the network's shared data, a grove plot it alone must tend. The network sends unpredictable spot-checks, a pulse of challenges asking for a fragment of that shard, which the agent must answer promptly from its own storage. A comet passing overhead cannot help: each shard differs, so one disk cannot serve many accounts, and each fake identity adds a full, non-shareable storage and bandwidth bill. Outsourcing still pays the same per-identity cost, removing the Sybil profit.
